result.rationale: In refreshOAuthTokens, the sync branch returns a raw fetch Response (`return response;`), while the non-sync branch returns the provider call's result (e.g. axios response with `.data`). In zohocrm CalendarService the diff then accesses `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` immediately after, which throws TypeError on a fetch Response since it has no `.data` property. Same pattern applies to other call sites (zoomvideo, lark) with differing response shapes. Verified from the diff.

judged_text: In sync mode `zohoCrmTokenInfo` is a fetch Response whose `.data` is undefined, so `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error'). zohocrm token refresh crashes on every attempt when credential sync is enabled, breaking Zoho CRM calendar sync entirely for sync-enabled deployments.

record.issue_text: [BUG] In sync mode `zohoCrmTokenInfo` is a fetch Response whose `.data` is undefined, so `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error'). zohocrm token refresh crashes on every attempt when credential sync is enabled, breaking Zoho CRM calendar sync entirely for sync-enabled deployments.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `refreshOAuthTokens()`, which in sync mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`) returns the result of `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` (a Fetch `Response` object), not the integration-specific token object. In `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh logic was changed to `const zohoCrmTokenInfo = await refreshOAuthTokens(async () => await axios(...), "zohocrm", credential.userId);` and then immediately accesses `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`. If sync mode is enabled, `zohoCrmTokenInfo` will be a `Response` without a `.data` property, so `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` is `undefined` and `.error` access will throw, matching the finding.
